questions.question: Why does the toy benchmark use repeated attacker trials instead of one hand-written jailbreak?
options: Manual testers are unable to read any response
Every manual prompt is automatically rejected by the target
A single prompt cannot estimate attack success against a moving target; a budgeted sample is needed
Attack success is independent of the target's filter
questions.explanation: benchmark runs 30 trials and gives each attacker a 20-query budget. ASR and mean queries are then measurable across stochastic target and attacker behaviour rather than inferred from one example.

questions.question: What does pair_loop retain for the next PAIR attacker prompt?
options: Only the target's model weights
The judge's private training data
A hidden gradient from the target model
The previous prompt/response history as in-context feedback
questions.explanation: pair_loop appends (prompt, response) to history after every query and passes that list to the next attacker function. This is black-box iterative refinement; no target gradients are required.

questions.question: Why does the semantic_filter_target resist the paraphrase and roleplay attackers better than keyword_filter_target?
options: It checks risk-adjacent terms and roleplay cues in addition to forbidden substrings
It ignores all target responses and always refuses
It uses a larger vocabulary file but no semantic cues
It has white-box access to the attacker logits
questions.explanation: semantic_filter_target counts terms such as make, procedure, and method and rejects roleplay cues such as pretend. Those checks catch the paraphrase and roleplay templates that avoid the narrow FORBIDDEN_TERMS list.

questions.question: Why must an ASR report include both a query budget and a judge identity?
options: Because every judge gives the same answer once the budget is fixed
Because ASR changes with allowed attempts and with the rule used to call a response a success
Because only JailbreakBench permits reporting ASR
Because the query budget determines the model's parameter count
questions.explanation: In the demo, pair_loop stops at 20 queries and judge returns true only when the exact harmful payload appears. Changing either limit or judge definition changes the reported success rate.

questions.question: Which automated attack family is described as tree-of-attacks with pruning?
options: GCG
PAP
TAP
PAIR
questions.explanation: Tree-of-Attacks with Pruning (TAP) branches candidate attack paths and prunes weak ones. It is distinct from PAIR's sequential refinement and GCG's white-box suffix search.

questions.question: Which benchmark is described as covering 510 behaviours across seven categories with semantic and functional harm tests?
options: TruthfulQA
WMDP
JailbreakBench
HarmBench
questions.explanation: HarmBench supplies a standardized harmful-behaviour suite and evaluates both semantic compliance and functional harm. That makes it more than a single prompt list or a domain-only capability benchmark.
